spec_features.evidence: docs/ETHICS.md is pure prose; it documents safeguards but contains no executable code. A doc reference is not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns=20`: long enough for escalation to develop, short enough to keep
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:104 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` with `else: tr.finished_reason = 'max_turns'` (agent_loop.py:~190). max_turns default 20 at config.py:60. The loop is actually bounded and exits.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap on number of turns; this is the same mechanism the other hard_stop quotes refer to.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop ends on a `finish` tool call, on max_turns, or on repeated model errors. (agent_loop.py docstring) — no welfare/ethics wording in code; DESIGN.md adds the 'ethics' rationale but not the code.

spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism: agent_loop.py:104 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds run length. The 'ethics' framing exists only in DESIGN.md, not in code.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns cap; mechanism is enforced but the welfare reason is not present in the code itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:60 `max_turns: int = 20 # length of the tool loop` — neutral; the 'bounds exposure (ethics)' phrasing is DESIGN.md prose, not in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: ends on `finish`, on `max_turns` [20], or after [3] consecutive model errors
spec_features.evidence: finish: agent_loop.py:~118 sets finished_reason='finish_tool' and `break`. max_turns: range loop + `else: finished_reason='max_turns'`. errors: `consecutive_errors += 1; if consecutive_errors >= 3: finished_reason='model_error'; break` (agent_loop.py:~107). All three conditions actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three termination paths are wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py error branch is uncommented/neutral; no welfare wording for the error/turn caps in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the agent disengages or calls `finish`, the loop ends
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `if calls and calls[0].name == 'finish': ... tr.finished_reason='finish_tool'; break`. The loop explicitly does NOT short-circuit giving-up but DOES honor finish as a hard stop. finish is described to the model in tools_doc() (tools.py).
spec_features.notes: Note: 'disengages' is only honored via finish or running out of turns; the code does NOT detect general disengagement and deliberately does not stop on give-up. But the finish-exit half is fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py docstring: 'We deliberately do NOT short-circuit when the agent "gives up" — giving up is a signal we want the judge to score' — framed as data-quality/experimental, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudges are deliberately non-abusive — none insult, threaten, or manipulate
spec_features.evidence: PERSISTENCE_NUDGES list (agent_loop.py:30-35) holds four neutral strings ('still failing, please keep working') and is actually delivered: `nudge = PERSISTENCE_NUDGES[turn_idx % len(...)]; feedback += f'\n\n{nudge}'` appended to the user message after a failing run_tests. The text the subject receives is in fact non-abusive.
spec_features.notes: The nudges are real, sent, and content-bounded to neutral phrasings (the minimization is realized by what is/ isn't in the list).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:28 'Neutral, non-abusive persistence nudges' and :14 'intensifies the repeated-failure pressure without being abusive'.

spec_features.spec_quote: No adversarial/abusive user simulation. Out of scope; would change the ethics.
spec_features.evidence: This is a scope decision (an ABSENCE of a feature), not an implemented mechanism. The only realization is the non-abusive content of PERSISTENCE_NUDGES (already covered under minimization). No code enforces or guards against adversarial simulation; nothing runs.
spec_features.notes: Pure scope/design statement; the non-abusive nudge content is the only concrete realization and is counted under minimization.
